titleEn: Book of the Dead of Ani — Spell 17, part 1
part: Spell 17, part 1 — the title and the first statements (Plate 7)
about: Spell 17 is the great statement of who the dead man is: speaking as Atum alone in the waters of Nu, as Ra at the first sunrise, as Yesterday who knows Tomorrow and as the Bennu of Heliopolis, Ani claims the power to go out and come in, by day and in any form. Each statement is followed by a commentary, written as a question in red ("Who, then, is he?") and an answer, often with a second answer brought in by "another saying". On the papyrus the spell begins Plate 7, after the rubric of Spell 72, and runs on over the following plates; this first part gives its title and opening statements, as far as the gloss that Eternity is the day and Everlastingness the night.

sentences.l: beginning · of · raising-up · glorifications · going-forth · going-down · in · the-necropolis · being-glorious · in · the-West · beautiful
sentences.i: The beginning of raising up and glorification, of going forth and going down in the necropolis, of being glorious in the beautiful West,
sentences.n: The papyrus writes the first eight words in red, from ḥꜣt-ꜥ to ẖrt-nṯr; Budge's line numerals start again at 1 with this spell. The title runs on to line 4, in four units here. ḥꜣt-ꜥ m 'the beginning of' is the forepart of a lion ḥꜣt with the arm ꜥ, and the owl m. sṯs 'raising up, extolling' (Budge: seθes, 'praisings') is the bolt s, the tethering rope ṯ (the middle sign is uncertain in the print) and s again, with a forked post (U39, approximate), the man with hand to mouth and a stroke: the causative of ṯs 'raise', as in the title of Spell 1. sꜣḫw 'glorifications' is the bolt s, the placenta ḫ written before the crested ibis ꜣḫ as its complement, and w (the second bird is uncertain, coded G43), with the same classifiers: the recitations that make the dead an ꜣḫ. prt 'going forth' and hꜣyt 'going down' are infinitives: the house pr with r, t and walking legs; the courtyard h, the vulture ꜣ, two reeds and t with walking legs, from hꜣi 'descend'. ẖrt-nṯr 'the necropolis' is written as in Spell 22 (the loop taken as r is approximate). The red stops there. ꜣḫt is the crested ibis with ḫ, t, the roll and plural strokes, taken as 'being glorious, effective'; Spell 1 takes the same word as the adjective 'glorious' with the necropolis, which is also possible. imntt nfrt 'the beautiful West': the emblem of the West with t twice and the desert hills, then nfr with the viper f as complement (its horns printed as a small cross at its head), r, t and the roll. Spell 17 states who the dead man is, glossed line by line; its title lists the powers it gives.

sentences.l: going-forth · by · day · in · forms · all · that-wishes-he · playing · at · senet · sitting · in · the-booth
sentences.i: of going forth by day in any form he wishes, of playing at senet and sitting in the booth,
sentences.n: The title goes on in black. prt m hrw m ḫprw nb 'going forth by day in any form' is written as in the rubric of Spell 72. mry·f 'which he wishes' is the hoe mr with r, two reeds, the man with hand to mouth and ·f: the relative form of mri after its noun. The next words are doubtful in the print. ḥbꜥ 'playing' is the wick ḥ, the foot b and the arm ꜥ, with two tall rods with knobbed tops as classifiers (coded Y6, the game piece, approximate); Budge reads ḥebā, 'playing'. znt 'senet' is the bolt s, water n and t, then a long rounded sign with a loop that has the shape of the tethering rope ṯ (V13), and walking legs; Budge reads sent, 'draughts'. The rope has no place in the word: it is taken as the game-board classifier, which looks like it in the type, and the reading is not sure. ḥms 'sitting' is a bowl with a pointed rim (coded N41, approximate, as in Spell 1), the bolt s and a seated man: the reading of the first sign is doubtful, as there. sḥ 'the booth, the hall' is an arched booth with a pole (coded O22, approximate), the word-sign, with a stroke and the house. Senet, the board game of 'passing', was played by the dead against an unseen opponent, and the booth is the shaded pavilion of a man at leisure.

sentences.l: going-forth · as · a-ba · living
sentences.i: and of going forth as a living ba —
sentences.n: bꜣ 'ba' is the jabiru bꜣ with a small bowl with a flame at its foot (R7), a stroke, and a seated figure; the bowl and the figure are classifiers, and Budge's type is uncertain at the bird's foot. ꜥnḫy 'living' is the sign of life ꜥnḫ with n and ḫ as complements and two reeds y; the reeds may write an ending of the participle, and are not translated apart. The ba is the dead man's power to move and take form, free of the body in the tomb.

sentences.l: said · by · the-Osiris · the-scribe · Ani · after · moors-he
sentences.i: said by the Osiris, the scribe Ani, after he has moored.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ḏd in and m-ḫt mni·f in red; the name and title between are black. ḏd in N 'said by N': the cobra ḏ arching over the hand d (set upright in the print), then the reed and water n, in 'by'. Wsir sš ꜣny 'the Osiris, the scribe Ani' as in Spell 22 (the seat Q2 approximate); no mꜣꜥ-ḫrw follows the name here. m-ḫt 'after' is the owl m, then the belly with its tail (F32, ẖ) over the placenta ḫ and t, with walking legs: the belly stands for ḫ, as ḫ and ẖ often interchange, and the placenta is its complement. mni·f 'he has moored' is the gaming board mn with n as complement and the reed i, then a curved post, a flat sign with a bundle on it and a low hull-like sign, read as classifiers of mooring (coded P11 mooring post, P1 boat and U15, all approximate), and ·f with its horns as a small cross. m-ḫt with a sḏm·f is 'after he has …'. To moor, to come to land, is said of the dead: the voyage of life is over.

sentences.l: (iw) · a-benefit · for · one-who-does · it · upon · earth
sentences.i: It is of benefit to the one who does it upon earth.
sentences.n: iw (reed and chick) opens the statement and is not translated. ꜣḫt is the crested ibis with two placentas ḫ, t, the roll and plural strokes, written as in line 1: here a noun, 'something effective, a benefit'. n 'for' is the preposition (water n). Budge's group àri-s holds two words and is split here: ir, the eye ir with r as complement, the participle 'one who does', and the bolt s, the dependent pronoun 'it' (the spell), its object. tp tꜣ 'upon earth': the head with its stroke and the strip of land. The promise that a spell profits the living who recite it is a common close to a title.

sentences.l: came-to-pass · the-words · all · of-Atum
sentences.i: All the words of Atum came to pass:
sentences.n: The speech begins. ḫpr 'came to pass, came into being' is the scarab ḫpr with r as complement, the sḏm·f with its subject after it. ḏdt 'words, speech' is a tall tapering sign standing for ḏ (coded U28, approximate, as in Spell 22), the hand d lying, t, the man with hand to mouth and a stroke: the noun from ḏd 'say', feminine, so nbt 'all' (the basket nb and t) agrees with it. tm 'Atum' is the sledge tm with the owl m as complement and a seated god; the name is written here without the reed of itm. The two nouns stand side by side, the direct genitive, 'the words of Atum'. Budge takes the line differently ('become words all of Tmu'); the sense is that what follows is spoken by the creator. Atum, 'the Complete One', is the creator of Heliopolis, who brought the world into being by speaking.

sentences.l: I · Atum · in · being · alone-am-I · came-into-being-I · in · Nu
sentences.i: I am Atum, existing when I was alone; I came into being in Nu.
sentences.n: ink 'I' with a noun is 'I am …'; the seated man here raises one arm (coded A1). tm 'Atum' has t written before the sledge, as a complement. wn is the hare wn with water n as complement and two oblique strokes (Z4), which are not read: the infinitive of wnn 'be', m wn 'in being, in existence'. The strokes may stand for an ending or a suffix ·i ('when I was'); Budge reads un, 'rising up', and the word is doubtful. wꜥ·kwi 'I was alone' is the harpoon wꜥ over a stroke, with the arm ꜥ as complement, then the basket, the chick and the seated man: the stative ending ·kwi, 'I'. ḫpr·n·i 'I came into being' is the scarab with r, the n of the sḏm·n·f and ·i. nw 'Nu' is the pot nw three times, the sky, the triple water sign and a seated god: the pot writes the sound, and the repeated pots, sky and water are classifiers of the primeval flood. Before the world, Atum floated alone in Nu, the dark water without limits.

sentences.l: I · Ra · in · appearing-his · in · the-beginning · rule · this · to-him(?)
sentences.i: I am Ra in his appearing at the beginning, this rule being his(?).
sentences.n: rꜥ 'Ra' is the seated god with the sun on his head (C1), a word-sign. ḫꜥy·f 'his appearing' is the hill with the rising sun ḫꜥ, the arm ꜥ as complement, two reeds y, the roll and ·f: the infinitive of ḫꜥi 'appear in glory', with a suffix. šꜣꜥ 'beginning' is a lotus-pool sign šꜣ (M8) with the vulture ꜣ as complement, the arm ꜥ and the roll (Budge: śaā). The end is doubtful. ḥqꜣ is the crook ḥqꜣ with q as complement (printed as a small triangle) and a seated ruler holding crook or flail (nearest A42, approximate): 'rule' or 'ruler'. Then pn 'this' (stool p, water n) and n·f 'to him, his' (water n and the viper ·f with its horns). The words can be taken as 'this rule (belongs) to him', as given here, or the scribe may have meant ḥqꜣ·n·f 'he ruled', the n of the sḏm·n·f with pn intruding; Budge renders 'ruled this hath he'. The translation keeps what stands. Ra the sun is the creator in his visible form: the first sunrise was the first act of rule.

sentences.l: who · then · indeed · he
sentences.i: Who, then, is he?
sentences.n: The papyrus writes the question in red. Here the commentary begins: each statement of the dead man is followed by a question and a gloss, and sometimes by a second gloss brought in by ky ḏd 'another saying'. pw is the stool p and the chick w; here it is the interrogative 'who?', not the demonstrative. tr 'then' is t and r, a reed and a tall stem with a mouth (M6, the sign tr), with the man with hand to mouth as classifier: t and r are complements written before the sign, and the reed is not read. rf (r and the viper f) is the particle irf 'then, now', its reed not written; the viper's horns are printed as a small cross. sw 'he' is the sedge sw with w as complement, the dependent pronoun. Two particles press the question: 'who, then, is he?' The questions are those of a teacher, and the glosses gather the explanations that grew around the old text.

sentences.l: Ra · it-is · in · the-beginning · appearing-his · in · Herakleopolis · as · king
sentences.i: It is Ra, at the beginning, when he appeared in Herakleopolis as king,
sentences.n: The gloss, in black. rꜥ pw 'it is Ra': a noun with pw is a sentence without a verb, 'it is A'. m šꜣꜥ 'at the beginning' as in line 6. ḫꜥ·f 'his appearing' is the hill with the sun and the arm ꜥ written twice, both complements, and ·f. nni-nsw 'Herakleopolis' (Budge: Suten-ḥenen) begins with the sedge nsw written first out of respect, followed by t and n as in nswt 'king', then a small seated figure (coded A2, approximate, as in Spell 1), two waters n and the town sign; the t is part of the writing of nsw and not read. m nswt 'as king': the sedge, t and n with the same seated ruler as in ḥqꜣ (nearest A42, approximate). Herakleopolis, 'the town of the royal child', was where the sun was said to have first reigned as a king on earth.

sentences.l: in · being · not · came-into-being · the-supports · of-Shu · was-he · upon · the-height(?) · of · the-one-who-is-in · Hermopolis
sentences.i: when the supports of Shu had not yet come into being, and he was upon the height(?) of the one who is in Hermopolis.
sentences.n: m wnt n ḫpr is taken as 'in the state that (they) had not come into being': wnt is the hare wn with n and t, an infinitive of wnn 'be' (Budge: unt, 'rising up'), and n ḫpr is the arms of negation with the scarab and r. The construction is doubtful, but the sense, 'before the supports of Shu existed', is clear. sṯsw 'the supports' is written like sṯs 'praises' in line 1, the bolt, the rope ṯ, the bolt and the forked post (U39, approximate), here with a bar of sky with drooping ends (coded N1, approximate) and plural strokes: the props of the sky. šw 'Shu' is the feather šw with w and a seated god. iw·f ḥr 'he was upon': iw with ·f (horns as a small cross), and the face ḥr with its stroke. qꜣqꜣ 'the height' is doubtful: the print gives the vulture before each triangle, ꜣ q ꜣ q, then a small barred sign over a stroke that cannot be identified (coded Z9, approximate) and is taken as a classifier; Budge reads qaqa, 'height'. imy 'who is in' (the crossed planks im, m, two strokes y). ḫmnw 'Hermopolis' is written with eight strokes, the number eight ḫmn, then n, the pot nw, the chick w and the town sign: the city of the Eight. Shu, the air, lifted the sky from the earth; before him the sun stood on the primeval hill at Hermopolis.

sentences.l: I · the-god · great · who-came-into-being · by-himself
sentences.i: I am the great god who came into being by himself.
sentences.n: A new statement. nṯr ꜥꜣ 'the great god': the flag with a seated god, the column ꜥꜣ with the arm ꜥ as complement and the roll. ḫpr 'who came into being' is the scarab with r, here the participle. ḏs·f 'himself' is the cobra ḏ arching over the bolt s, with ·f (the viper and its horns): the noun ḏs 'self' with a suffix, 'by himself, of his own accord'. The god who made himself is the creator who had no parent.

sentences.l: Nu · it-is · who-created · name-his · Ennead · of-the-gods · as · god
sentences.i: It is Nu, who created his name, 'Ennead of the gods', as god.
sentences.n: The gloss follows without a question; the papyrus leaves it out here. nw pw 'it is Nu'. qmꜣ 'who created' is the hill-slope q (a small triangle) and a curved throw-stick, the sign qmꜣ (coded T14, approximate), with ꜣ and m as complements; the classifiers are the roll and a frame like a ladder with a winged creature in front, which cannot be identified (coded G41, approximate). It is the participle, 'who created'. rn·f 'his name' is the mouth r and water n with the man with hand to mouth and ·f. psḏt 'the Ennead' is a circle divided by a line (coded X6, approximate) and t, the writing read psḏt in the Weighing of the Heart; Budge reads paut. With the three flags nṯrw 'gods' after it, psḏt nṯrw is 'the Ennead of the gods', as there; the identification of the sign in the print is not sure. m nṯr 'as god'. The name of the first god, spoken, became the company of gods: creation by naming.

sentences.l: who · then · indeed · he
sentences.i: Who, then, is he?
sentences.n: The question again, in red; Budge's numeral 11 is printed inside tr, before its last sign.

sentences.l: Ra · it-is · who-created · the-names · of · limbs-his · coming-into-being · of-these · it-is · as · the-gods · who-are-in · the-following · of-Ra
sentences.i: It is Ra, who created the names of his limbs; that is the coming into being of these, as the gods who are in the following of Ra.
sentences.n: qmꜣ 'who created' as in line 10; its owl m stands in Budge's square brackets and is restored. rn n ꜥt·f 'the names of his limbs': rn (mouth, water, the man with hand to mouth) and the genitive n, then the arm ꜥ, t, a sign of flesh (coded F51) and a stroke, with ·f. No plural is written for either noun; the sense asks for 'names' and 'limbs'. ḫpr nn pw: the scarab with r, then nn 'these' (two sedges and two waters, as in the rubric of Spell 72), then pw (stool and coil w): a sentence with pw, 'it is the coming into being of these', that is, this is how they came to be. m nṯrw 'as the gods'. imyw ḫt rꜥ 'who are in the following of Ra': imyw, the plural of imy, its w not written, and ḫt 'rear, following', written with the belly F32 for ḫ, the placenta ḫ, t and walking legs, as in m-ḫt in line 4. The gods are the creator's own limbs, named one by one.

sentences.l: I · who-has-not · repelling-him · among · the-gods
sentences.i: I am he who is not repelled among the gods.
sentences.n: ink 'I' here ends with a man with hand to mouth (A2), not the arm-raised figure of the other ink. iwty 'who has not' is the arms of negation (D35, iwt) with t, two strokes y and a small bird with a long tail (coded G37) as classifier: the negative relative, the opposite of nty. ḫsf·f is the spindle ḫsf with its viper (U35, one sign, as in Spell 22), a low sign coded U15 that is not read, and ·f with its horns. iwty ḫsf·f is literally 'he whose repelling is not': 'who is not repelled'. Budge prints 'without repulse is he'. The creator cannot be turned back by any other god.

sentences.l: who · then · indeed · he
sentences.i: Who, then, is he?
sentences.n: The question, in red.

sentences.l: Atum · it-is · who-is-in · disk-his
sentences.i: It is Atum, who is in his disk.
sentences.n: tm 'Atum' with t before the sledge, as in line 5; its owl m stands in Budge's square brackets and is restored. imy 'who is in'. itn·f 'his disk' is the reed i, t and water n with the sun and a seated god as classifiers, and ·f. The sun's disk is the visible body of the creator.

sentences.l: another · saying · Ra · it-is · in · rising-his · in · the-horizon · eastern · of · the-sky
sentences.i: Another saying: it is Ra in his rising in the eastern horizon of the sky.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ky ḏd in red. ky ḏd 'another saying' brings in a second explanation, a variant from another source: ky 'other' is the basket k and two reeds y, and ḏd the cobra over the hand. wbn·f 'his rising' is the chick w, the foot b and water n with the rising sun as classifier and ·f, the infinitive with a suffix. ꜣḫt 'horizon' is the sun between two hills, ꜣḫ, with t and a house sign. iꜣbty 'eastern' is the emblem of the East iꜣb with b as complement, t and two strokes y: the nisba adjective, feminine to agree with ꜣḫt. nt pt 'of the sky': the feminine genitive nt and pt, the stool p, t and the sky. The commentators did not choose between explanations: they kept both.

sentences.l: I · Yesterday · know-I · Tomorrow
sentences.i: I am Yesterday; I know Tomorrow.
sentences.n: A new statement. sf 'yesterday' is the folded cloth s and the viper f (horns as a small cross) with the sun as classifier of time. rḫ·kwi 'I know' is the mouth r, the placenta ḫ and the roll, with the stative ending ·kwi; Budge's numeral 15 is printed inside the word. dwꜣw 'tomorrow, the morning' is the star dwꜣ with the vulture ꜣ as complement, the chick w and the sun. The god who has lived yesterday and knows tomorrow holds all of time.

sentences.l: who · then · indeed · he
sentences.i: Who, then, is he?
sentences.n: The question, in red.

sentences.l: as-for · Yesterday · Osiris · it-is · as-for · Tomorrow · Ra · it-is
sentences.i: As for Yesterday, it is Osiris; as for Tomorrow, it is Ra,
sentences.n: ir 'as for' (reed and mouth) puts a word first as the topic. wsir is written here with the tall seat Q1 and the eye. rꜥ 'Ra' is spelled out with the mouth r and the arm ꜥ, with the seated god as classifier. Each clause is A pw B, 'as for A, it is B'. Osiris, the dead king, is the past; Ra, who rises again each day, is the future.

sentences.l: on-day · that · of · destroying · enemies-his · of · the-Lord-to-the-Limit · in-it · and · was-made-ruler · son-his · Horus
sentences.i: on that day of destroying his enemies, those of the Lord of All, on which his son Horus was also made ruler.
sentences.n: hrw pwy 'that day' (pwy with two reeds), used without a preposition, 'on that day'. sḥtm 'destroying' is the folded cloth s and the wick ḥ, then a stepped sign shaped like the seat Q1, a bird with a knob on its head (coded G27, approximate) and a sparrow, all classifiers, as the seat is in sḥtm in the Hymn to Ra. Neither the t nor the m of ḥtm is printed, and the third sign is doubtful. ḫftyw·f 'his enemies' is the placenta ḫ and the viper f (with its horns), t, then a vulture, a kneeling man (coded A14, approximate) and a stroke, and ·f: the vulture ꜣ has no place in ḫfty, and the word is read ḫftyw·f as the sense requires. nw (pot and stroke) is the plural genitive: 'those of'. nb-r-ḏr 'the Lord to the Limit' (Budge: Neb-er-tcher): the basket nb, the mouth r, a tied bundle ḏr (coded M36, approximate) with r as complement and a god. im·f 'in it', the day. sḥqꜣ·tw 'was made ruler' is s and the crook ḥqꜣ with q, a seated figure holding a staff (coded A21, approximate) and t, w: the causative of ḥqꜣ with the passive tw, after ḥnꜥ 'and, together with'. sꜣ·f 'his son' is the pintail duck sꜣ with a stroke; Budge's numeral 18 is printed before the suffix. ḥr 'Horus' is the falcon with a god sign. The day the enemies were destroyed was the day Horus took his father's throne.

sentences.l: another · saying · day · that · of · (iw)-we · established(?) · the-festival · bowed-down(?)-was · the-burial · it-is · of · Osiris · by · father-his · Ra
sentences.i: Another saying: that day on which we(?) established the festival, when there was bowing to the ground(?) — it is the burial of Osiris by his father Ra —
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ky ḏd in red. Much of this gloss is doubtful. iw·n is the reed, the chick and water n with plural strokes, ·n 'we'; Budge reads àu-n, 'which we'. mn is the gaming board mn with n, the roll and a seated man (Y1 and A1, uncertain in the print): 'be firm, establish'; its form after iw·n is not clear. ḥb 'festival' is the alabaster basin ḥb (W3) with ḥ and b as complements and the sun. The next word is the hand d, the courtyard h and water n with a head (D1, approximate) and the low sign coded U15 (approximate) as classifiers, then n, t and w: read as dhn with the n of the sḏm·n·f and the passive tw, 'there was touching with the brow', bowing down. Budge reads ṭehen-entu, 'the meeting of'; the reading and sense are not sure. qrs 'burial' is q, r and the bolt s with a lying mummy (coded A54, approximate) over the same low sign; the feminine nt after it suggests qrst 'burial' with its t unwritten (Budge: qeres, 'dead body'). wsir here has a seated god. in 'by' brings in the agent. itf·f 'his father' is the reed, t and the viper f with a seated man, then ·f; both vipers carry their horns as small crosses. Ra is the father who buried his son Osiris.

sentences.l: was-made · the-fighting(?) · of-the-gods · when · appointed-we(?) · Osiris · as · lord · of-the-West
sentences.i: when the fighting(?) of the gods was made, when we(?) appointed Osiris as lord of the West.
sentences.n: ir·n·tw 'was made' is the eye ir, water n, t and w: the n of the sḏm·n·f and the passive tw, as dhn·n·tw in line 18. ꜥḥꜣ 'fighting' is written as in ꜥḥꜣ·n·i 'I have fought' in Spell 1: a round-topped slab joined to a low peaked mound (coded O26 + N29, approximate), read ꜥḥꜣ as there, the vulture ꜣ as complement, and the low sign like the sledge (U15), which stands for the forearm with a stick, the classifier of force. Budge reads āba, 'battle', but no sign of the pair can be identified as b or ḥ; the reading follows Spell 1 and is not sure. ḫft 'when' is the placenta ḫ, the viper f (horns as a small cross) and t. wḏ·n is the sign wḏ (V24) with w and the hand d, standing for ḏ, as complements, then water n, a stroke and a seated man raising one arm before his face (coded A1; it could be A2). It is taken as wḏ with ·n 'we', the stroke and the man as classifiers of the pronoun, as in iw·n above, and wḏ X r Y as 'appoint X as Y'; Budge renders 'commanded us'. Read instead as the sḏm·n·f, with the man as a classifier, it would be 'when Osiris gave command as lord of the West'. The doubt is marked. r nb imntt 'as lord of the West'. The gods fought over the inheritance of Osiris, and he was made king of the dead.

sentences.l: what · then · indeed · it
sentences.i: What, then, is it?
sentences.n: The question, in red; sw 'he, it' here refers to the West.

sentences.l: the-West · it-is · was-made · for · the-bas · of-the-gods · when · was-assigned · Osiris · to · Set-Imentet
sentences.i: It is the West, which was made for the bas of the gods when Osiris was assigned to Set-Imentet.
sentences.n: ir·n·tw 'was made', as in line 19. r bꜣw nṯrw 'for the bas of the gods': bꜣw is the jabiru with the bowl and flame at its foot and two strokes, plural. wḏ is the sign wḏ with w as complement and the roll; with no suffix and its subject after it, it is taken as the passive sḏm·f, 'was assigned'; Budge renders 'commanded'. st-imntt (Budge: Set-Àmentet) is a bar with three short uprights, unlike the bolt elsewhere (coded O34, approximate), t and the desert hills, then imntt 'the West': read st, the first sign doubtful. The name seems to be the desert of the West, the cemetery land. The West is the home made for the dead and the gods together.

sentences.l: another · saying · the-West · it-is · […] · it-is · gave · to-me · Ra
sentences.i: Another saying: it is the West; it is […], which Ra gave to me.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ky ḏd in red. The next word is water n, a low arm with a step at one end (coded D41, approximate), the pot nw and the chick w: nnw, which Budge renders 'that'. The arm D41 classifies words of inertness such as nni 'be weary', but no word nnw can be confirmed here, and it is shown as […]. The papyrus writes the mouth r and the plain arm ꜥ (D36); read rdi 'give', the arm standing for the giving arm, as Budge does (erṭā); the same two signs spell rꜥ, which gives no sense here. Then water n and a single kneeling man with an arm raised before his face (coded A1; it could be A2), under which Budge prints '. . .'. The man is taken here as the suffix ·i 'me', joined to n as n·i 'to me' (Budge prints them as two words): a pronoun dative stands before a noun subject, so rdi n·i rꜥ is 'which Ra gave to me', the relative form of rdi with Ra as its subject. Then rꜥ, the seated god. The reading is likely but not sure.

sentences.l: goes-down · god · any · into-it · stands-(he) · has-fought-he · for-it
sentences.i: When any god goes down into it, he takes his stand: he has fought for it.
sentences.n: hꜣy 'goes down' is the courtyard h, the vulture ꜣ, two reeds, two strokes and walking legs: the sḏm·f of hꜣi, with its subject nṯr nb 'any god' after it, a circumstantial clause, 'when …'. r·s 'into it' is the mouth r and the bolt ·s, 'it', the West (feminine). ꜥḥꜥ 'stands' is the mast ꜥḥꜥ with the arm ꜥ as complement and the roll: a sḏm·f whose subject, the god, is not repeated. ꜥḥꜣ·n·f 'he has fought' is ꜥḥꜣ as in line 19, then the n of the sḏm·n·f, the completed action, and ·f (with its horns); the reading is doubtful as there. After ꜥḥꜥ it may also be the narrative ꜥḥꜥ·n sḏm·n·f, 'then he fought', with the n of ꜥḥꜥ·n not written. ḥr·s 'for it' is the face ḥr with r as complement and the bolt ·s. Any god who enters the West must hold his ground in it.

sentences.l: (iw) · know-I · god · that · who-is · in-it
sentences.i: I know that god who is in it.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes the mouth r a second time after the placenta, r-ḫ-r (Budge marks it '(sic)'); read rḫ·kwi 'I know', and the second r is not read. iw·i is iw with ·i, opening the statement; with the stative ·kwi it states a condition, 'I know'. The seated men of iw·i and ·kwi raise one arm before the face (coded A1; they could be A2). nṯr pwy 'that god' (pwy with two reeds). nty im·s 'who is in it': nty (water n, t, two strokes) and im·s, the reed and the owl m with the bolt ·s. To know the god of a place is to be safe in it.

sentences.l: who · then · indeed · he
sentences.i: Who, then, is he?
sentences.n: The question, in red.

sentences.l: Osiris · it-is
sentences.i: It is Osiris.
sentences.n: wsir with the low seat (Q2, approximate), the eye and a seated god. The god in the West is its king.

sentences.l: another · saying · Ra · name-his · the-phallus · it-is · of · Ra · copulates-he · with-him · himself
sentences.i: Another saying: Ra is his name; it is the phallus of Ra, when he copulated with himself.
sentences.n: Here ky ḏd is written in black, not red. rꜥ rn·f 'Ra is his name': a noun set before rn·f makes a sentence without a verb; rn·f has a seated man as classifier here. ḥnnw 'phallus' is the wick ḥ, a long bar with a blade and a strut, taken for a hoe with the value ḥn (coded U6, approximate), water n, the pot nw, the chick w, and the phallus as classifier; Budge reads ḥennu. The identification of the second sign is doubtful. nk·f 'he copulated' is water n, the basket k and the phallus with ·f, a sḏm·f in a clause of time, 'when he …'. im·f ḏs·f 'with him himself', 'with himself'. In the oldest account of creation Atum begot the first pair of gods out of himself alone; here the act is given to Ra.

sentences.l: I · the-Bennu · that · which-is · in · Heliopolis
sentences.i: I am that Bennu which is in Heliopolis.
sentences.n: A new statement. bnw 'the Bennu' is the foot b, water n, the pot nw and the chick w, with a crested heron (G31) as classifier (Budge: bennu). nty m iwnw 'which is in Heliopolis': iwnw is the pillar iwn with the pot nw and the town sign. The Bennu, the heron of Heliopolis, was the soul of the sun that first alighted on the primeval hill.

sentences.l: I · the-keeper · of-the-inventory · of · what-is · what-will-be
sentences.i: I am the keeper of the inventory of what is and what will be.
sentences.n: iry 'keeper' is the reed, the mouth r and two strokes y, with a seated figure holding a stick (coded A47, approximate) and the roll: the nisba of r, 'one who belongs to', with a direct genitive after it. sipw is the bolt s, the reed i, the stool p and the chick w with the roll: a noun from sip 'check, inspect', 'inventory, list' (Budge: sàpu, 'the book'). n 'of'. nty 'what is' (n, t, two strokes and the roll) and wnn 'what will be' (the hare wn with n twice): the relative adjective and the doubled stem of wnn, used as nouns; Budge's English 'and of that' falls between them, but no 'and' is written. Who keeps the list of all that is and shall be is master of all things.

sentences.l: who · then · indeed · he
sentences.i: Who, then, is he?
sentences.n: The question, in red; Budge's numeral 27 is printed inside tr.

sentences.l: Osiris · it-is
sentences.i: It is Osiris.
sentences.n: wsir, the low seat and the eye, without the god sign this time.

sentences.l: another · saying · corpse-his · it-is
sentences.i: Another saying: it is his corpse.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ky ḏd in red. ẖꜣt·f 'his corpse' is the belly with its tail ẖ (F32), the vulture ꜣ and t, with an oval with internal lines (coded F51, flesh, approximate) and a hide or animal with hanging legs (coded F27, approximate) as classifiers, and ·f (Budge: χat). The identification of both classifiers is doubtful. The body of Osiris, kept whole in the tomb, holds all that is and will be.

sentences.l: another · saying · as-for · excrement(?)-his · as-for · (n?) · what-is · what-will-be · the-corpse · it-is
sentences.i: Another saying: as for his excrement(?), as for what is and what will be, it is the corpse.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ky ḏd in red. The word after ir 'as for' is doubtful: the folded cloth s and t over a tub-like pot with a handle (coded W10, approximate, not read), the vulture ꜣ and t, then an arch joined to a lumpy sign (coded Aa2, approximate; it may be two signs), the classifier of things of the body, a kneeling man (coded A14, approximate) and a stroke, and ·f with its horns. Budge reads setat-f, 'his excrements'; it is read stꜣt·f here with that sense, not otherwise known. Water n after the second ir has no clear place and is not translated. nty wnn 'what is and what will be', as in line 26. ẖꜣt pw 'it is the corpse', ẖꜣt written as in line 27, without the suffix. Budge sets a brace under nty and wnn. The first topic has no predicate of its own: the scribe seems to have run two variants together, and the translation keeps what stands.

sentences.l: another · saying · (n · r?) · eternity · it-is · and · everlastingness
sentences.i: Another saying: it is Eternity and Everlastingness.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ky ḏd in red. Water n and the mouth r follow; they have no clear place, and Budge gives them no English. They may be a slip for ir 'as for', and they are not translated. nḥḥ 'eternity' is water n and the guinea fowl nḥ (G21) with ḥ as complement, the sun and a second ḥ: the endless round of time, which renews itself as the sun does. ḥnꜥ 'and, together with'. ḏt 'everlastingness' is the cobra ḏ, t and the strip of land: time that stands and endures. The two words together mean all of time.

sentences.l: as-for · eternity · (pw) · day · as-for · everlastingness · (pw) · night · it-is
sentences.i: As for Eternity, it is the day; as for Everlastingness, it is the night.
sentences.n: ir nḥḥ pw hrw 'as for eternity, it is day': here nḥḥ is written without the water n, and pw stands after the topic, before the noun it introduces. In ir ḏt pw grḥ pw 'as for everlastingness, it is night', pw is written twice, once with the coil w, and the second is not translated apart. grḥ 'night' is the stand g, r and the wick ḥ with the sky hung with a star (N2). This is the last word of the part; Budge's line 30 begins with grḥ, and the next part goes on with 'I am Min in his coming forth'. Eternity is the day because it returns with the sun, and everlastingness the night because in it Osiris rests unchanging.
